entries.title: The compass
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-07 (the game's CLAUDE.md, "The map")
entries.summary: North colder, south richer and settled, east rivers and trade, west open ocean and the unknown. Distance sets how hard; direction sets what kind.
entries.body:
**The compass means something; the details are generated** (Robin). North colder, south richer and settled ("England in
the south"), east rivers and trade, west open ocean and the unknown. Distance from home sets how hard a place is,
direction what kind. The map shows nothing until it is seen.

The lore keeps the same rule. Every family, every legend and every name pool has a home region: [[world.home]],
[[world.north]], [[world.south]], [[world.east]], [[world.west]]. The generator places them by it.

SAID: "East is trade. West is nothing but sea." — a villager on the big island
SAID: "Colder north of here than you would think." — a villager on the big island

entries.title: The hero
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 ("The player picks" the name; why he came to the island is "never explained"; he drifts ashore or wakes beside a broken boat)
entries.summary: Nobody knows who he is or why he was at sea, and the game never says. The player names him. He wakes on a beach with nothing, next to a broken boat.
entries.body:
The hero wakes on the beach of the starter island beside a broken boat, with nothing in his hands. **Why he was at sea is
never explained.** The player fills it in, or doesn't. **The player picks his name.**

What the world knows of him is only what he does from that morning on. That is the point. Every other person in the Isles
comes with a family, a ring and a story. He comes with none, and makes all three.

PROPOSED: **People notice what he lacks.** A stranger with no ring, no kin and no ship is unusual enough to talk about.
Arnor's first words are about it. Villagers ask, and get no answer. Folk on the big island say the sea "gave him up", the way
[[god.ran|Rán]] sometimes throws a drowned man back. None of this needs an answer from the game. It only needs people to
wonder aloud.

PROPOSED: **Bynames on top of his name.** The player's name is his given name. The world adds a byname from what he does
(see [[story.bynames]]), heard behind his back first.

entries.title: The night Ormr came
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (the hero finds the village with the survivor there, scavenging and fixing what he can; he is alive because the raiders always leave a survivor to tell the stories of the vile Viking who raided the town)
entries.summary: Two winters ago Ormr Midgardbane's longship came up the sound to the steading on the starter island. He burned it and left one man alive to tell it: Arnor, the smith.
entries.body:
**Robin's start:** the hero comes to the burnt village while the survivor is there, scavenging and fixing what he can. He is
alive because the raiders always leave a survivor, someone to tell the stories of the vile Viking who raided the town.

**What happened** (told in Arnor's approved lines). Two winters ago, in autumn, [[person.ormr|Ormr Midgardbane]]'s longship came up the sound to
the steading of [[person.thorgunna|Thorgunna]]. Ormr asked for wool and silver, as he always does: *"Pay, or burn."*
Thorgunna would not pay. They burned the hall. Thorgunna and her sons died at its door. Some of the steading's people were
taken for thralls. Some went with Ormr of their own will. The rest are under the turf behind the hall.

**The one who was left.** When it was over, Ormr's men found the smith, [[person.arnor|Arnor]], alive in his
smithy. Ormr looked at him a long time and said, *"Somebody has to tell it."* They broke his forge and left him. Arnor has
told it ever since, to every trader who puts in for water, because there is nobody else to tell it to, and because Ormr
knew he would. He hates that most of all.

FOUND, NEVER TOLD: None of this is narrated. It is found in pieces: Arnor's lines; the graves and their markers; what
villagers on other islands say of Ormr (each place has its own survivor, and its own version); and, much later, what
Ormr's own crew says about the custom.

entries.title: Chapter 1: What the Sea Gave Up
entries.decided: Robin (the starter island, the wreck, the broken steading, the first friendly person, the first legendary Viking heard of: 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-14). Robin, 2026-10-16: the hero's past is never explained and the player names him; he drifts ashore or wakes beside a broken boat; the survivor Arnor is in the burnt village scavenging and fixing what he can, left alive to tell the story of Ormr Midgardbane.
entries.summary: The starter island. A stranger with no name and no past wakes beside a broken boat, finds a burnt steading with one man left alive in it to tell the story, makes a home of the ruin, and leaves on a raft, east.
entries.tags: the starter island, the wreck, Arnor, the raft
entries.body:
**What it holds (the game's):** the wreck on the beach, the broken steading, the survivor, the first home (Comfort 4), the
first night and its wolves, the raft. No ring. The rule: the unprepared are weak, the prepared are fine; night is dangerous
and home with a fire is safe.

**Robin's start (2026-10-16):** the hero wakes on the beach beside a broken boat, or drifts ashore, with nothing. Why he was
at sea is never explained, and the player names him. Inland is a burnt village, and in it the survivor, **Arnor**, the
smith, scavenging and fixing what he can. Ormr Midgardbane's raiders always leave one alive to tell the story.

PROPOSED: **The beats.**

| Beat | Where it is found |
| --- | --- |
| **The wreck.** Nothing in your hands, and nothing to say who you are. | The game's start. |
| **The smoke.** A thin column over the trees: Arnor's fire. | The game's `start-loop.md` idea. |
| **The one who was left.** A man in the ruin, mending a door for a house with no roof. He looks at you a long time, and tells it. | Arnor's meet lines ([[line.arnor.meet]]). |
| **The graves.** Arnor says who lies in each, and the crooked runes on Thorgunna's stone. | The graves behind the hall ([[line.arnor.graves]]). |
| **The golden glint.** In an oak grove at midsummer dusk. Nobody explains it. | [[legend.gullinbursti]] |
| **The first night.** Wolves; the fire keeps them off; Arnor says one line about the dark. | The game's first night. |
| **The raft, and east.** "Then east, past the big island. That is where his sails went." | Arnor's teach lines; the banner. |

**The way on:** Ormr's name, the direction east, and Arnor at the shore as you go.

entries.title: Chapter 2: The Ring under the Hill
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-06 (the big events: copper, the troll and the cave, building an actual village, the arm ring), 2026-10-16 (Hårungen; and the dead Viking in the cave connects to someone met earlier: maybe an old man in the village who went there with his brother long ago and tells stories of the troll)
entries.summary: The big island. Copper, the troll and his young, an old man's story at the village fire, the first village of the hero's own, and at the back of the troll's cave, the old man's brother and his ring.
entries.tags: the big island, the troll, copper, the arm ring, the hird
entries.body:
**What it holds (the game's):** a big island with a small mountain; copper; the troll's cave and Hårungen; the hamlet; the
claim stone and the first hirdman joining; the bronze ring from the dead Viking and the carver's bench; the first boat. The
rule: heavier metal beats you; the troll is heavier than you until you have copper and the ring.

**Robin's connection (2026-10-16):** the dead Viking in the cave is tied to someone the hero meets first: maybe an old man in
the village on the big island, who went to the cave with his brother long ago, and tells stories of the troll.

PROPOSED: **The beats.** The big island is where the hero stops being a stranger. He finds the village that paid Ormr in wool
and is still standing, an old man who has been inside the hill, and, at the back of the troll's cave, the end of the old
man's story.

| Beat | Where it is found |
| --- | --- |
| **The village that paid.** *"Pay, and they leave. Fight, and they burn."* | The hamlet's lines (in the game). |
| **Old Aslak's story.** At the village fire: the little ones that bonk the stone, the father who comes when they cry, the brother who ran the wrong way. | [[person.aslak]], [[line.aslak.story]] |
| **Kolbein.** A villager who asks whether the smith on the little island is still alive, and does not want the answer. | [[person.kolbein]], one of the generated villagers. |
| **The troll's family.** Hårungen, friendly until struck; the father who comes for them. Exactly as Aslak said. | [[being.harungen]], [[being.bergtroll]] |
| **Hogni.** Behind the lair, bones in rotted mail, a bronze ring, and a line scratched low on the rock. | [[person.hogni]], [[place.troll-cave]] |
| **The ring given twice.** Aslak will not take it back: *"Keep it. He'd want it to see daylight."* | [[line.aslak.ring]] |
| **The ring and the blood.** The first rune, cut with the hero's own blood. | The carver's bench. |
| **The stone raised.** The first hirdman, the first village of his own. | The claim stone; Arnor joins. |
| **A sail on the horizon.** Striped, big, sailing calmly through a squall that keeps everyone else ashore. Not followed. | The idea bank's "seen at sea". |

**The way on:** the boat needs a sail, and the village talks of the hall in the south with silver on its walls.

entries.title: Chapter 3: The Silver Hall
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07 (the second biome, the southern lowlands; the first Viking ship; the first raid; a human jarl holds the silver ring, won by raiding his hall)
entries.summary: The southern lowlands. The first Viking ship, the first raid, and Jarl Önund the Prime-signed, who was Ormr's captain the night the steading on the starter island burned.
entries.tags: the lowlands, the first raid, the silver ring
entries.game: the battle test scene; not spawned in the game yet
entries.body:
**What it holds (the game's):** the settled southern lowlands, walled towns, churches, a manor; iron; the karve; the raid,
which everything in this chapter revolves round; the silver ring from a human jarl, won by raiding his hall.

PROPOSED: **The story.** The hero becomes a raider, and has to decide what kind. Ormr leaves one alive to tell it. The hero
may leave everyone, or no one. The big raid is the **Silver Hall** of [[person.onund|Jarl Önund the Prime-signed]], who wears
the silver ring, and who rowed for Ormr the night Thorgunna's steading burned. If Arnor is in the hird, he knows Önund's face.

| Beat | Where it is found |
| --- | --- |
| **The first church.** A priest who will not fight. *"He will know who took it."* | A church raid. |
| **A thrall who knows Arnor.** One of the burnt steading's people, freed in a raid. | [[story.threads]] |
| **Ragnhild Red-Sail** raiding the same coast, the same week. | [[person.ragnhild]] at sea or in a town. |
| **Önund's hall**, and his pendant that is a cross from the front and a hammer from the side. | The Silver Hall raid. |
| **The silver ring**, and what Önund says when he loses it: that Ormr's Serpent story was different when he was drunk. | The ring-holder's last lines. |

**The way on:** Önund, beaten, says where Ormr winters: up an eastern river, past the Kaupang.

entries.title: Arnor
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (named Arnor; the village smith; when the hero comes he is in the burnt village scavenging and fixing what he can; he is alive because the raiders always leave a survivor to tell the stories). His place in the game (the story, teaching the raft, the first hirdman) is Brokk's, renamed.
entries.summary: The smith of the burnt steading on the starter island, left alive by Ormr Midgardbane to tell the story. He fixes what he can, and tells it to everyone.
entries.game: today brokkLines, brokkState (templates/game.html); the first hirdman (src/hird.js)
entries.body:
Arnor was the smith of [[person.thorgunna|Thorgunna]]'s steading. When the hero comes over the rise he is there in the ruin,
scavenging and fixing what he can. He is alive because Ormr Midgardbane's raiders always leave one survivor, someone to
tell the stories of the Viking who raided the place (Robin, 2026-10-16).

PROPOSED: **Who he is.** An ordinary man: short, broad, forty, burn-scarred forearms, with a smith's habit of measuring
everything by fire and iron. Ormr's men broke his forge and left him standing in it. He has spent two winters mending what
can be mended (a roof here, a door there) for nobody to live in. He tells the story of the burning to every trader who puts
in for water, because he cannot help it, and because Ormr knew he would. That is the part he hates.

PROPOSED: **What the hero is to him.** The first person in two winters who stays. Arnor teaches him the house, the hearth and
the raft, the way he would teach an apprentice: by telling him what is missing, never what to do. When the hero raises a claim
stone, Arnor is the first to join it. He wears bronze, a smith's ring.

PROPOSED: **What he wants.** Not revenge: he has seen Ormr's men and knows better. He wants the steading to have people in it
again. [[story.threads|The taken]] are his people. Each one the hero brings home, he greets by name.

SAID: "Somebody has to tell it, he said. So here I am, telling it." — Arnor (proposed, see line.arnor.meet)

entries.title: Ormr Midgardbane
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (the raider, replacing Ragnar Ironside: "Ormr Midgardbane. His name stems from stories that the midgårdsorm fears and respects him, leaving him to travel the ocean without worries of storm. Some say he can even call upon the snake to control the seas."; he always leaves a survivor to tell the stories)
entries.summary: The sea-king who burned the steading on the starter island. Folk say the World Serpent fears and respects him, that no storm touches his ship, and that he can call the Serpent up to rule the sea. He always leaves one alive to tell it.
entries.tags: legendary viking, the tale of Ormr, the Serpent, the high seat
entries.game: today "Ragnar" in brokkLines, FOLK_LINES, ROLES.elder (src/village.js) and the "Ragnar sailed east" banner
entries.body:
**Robin's words:** *"Ormr Midgardbane. His name stems from stories that the midgårdsorm fears and respects him, leaving him to
travel the ocean without worries of storm. Some say he can even call upon the snake to control the seas."* And his raiders
always leave a survivor, someone to tell the stories of the vile Viking who raided the town.

*Ormr* is simply the Old Norse word for a serpent. Folk find that fitting.

PROPOSED: **Why he leaves one alive.** Ormr knows the oldest verse in the Isles by heart: *"Cattle die, kinsmen die, you
yourself will die; but the word of fame never dies for the one who earns it well"* (the *Hávamál*, verse 77). He means to be
that word. A survivor is a mouth. Every place he burns tells his story for him, and every story makes the next place pay.
*"Pay, or burn"* works because everyone has already heard what "burn" means.

**Where the name came from: nobody knows** (Robin, 2026-10-16). Everybody has heard a different story, and no one knows
what is true, or whether any of it is. What everybody knows is the name, and that his ship crosses the seas unharmed.

PROPOSED: **The stories folk tell.** Each survivor Ormr leaves tells it a little differently, so the Isles have many versions,
and each person who tells one believes it:

- **His own:** he met the Serpent at the edge of the world and stared it down, and it has feared him since. (His crew.)
- **The pilot's:** he sailed with King Hrólf, and when the king hooked the Serpent, the young Ormr cut the line, as the giant
  Hymir cut Thor's. The Serpent has owed him ever since. (Ásgaut, and nobody believes him.)
- **The ring:** he wears the lost [[thing.serpent-ring|Serpent Ring]] under his sleeve, and the Serpent will not harm its
  own image. (The south, and Yrsa the Wise.)
- **The sea's child:** his mother was one of Rán's daughters, the waves, and the sea will not drown its own. (Fishermen.)
- **No story at all:** there is no Serpent, he is simply the best seaman alive, and very lucky. (Ragnhild Red-Sail.)

The game never says which is true. Each is found where it is told.

PROPOSED: **How he is met.** He is heard of on every island, from the survivors he leaves and from people who paid. His sail
is seen on the horizon in chapter 2 or 3: a ship sailing calmly through weather that keeps everyone else ashore. His
ship-fort in the east is chapter 4. The last meeting is at sea, in the west, where the swell starts.

SAID: "Ragnar's men came by last winter. We paid them in wool and they left." — a villager on the big island (in the game today; the name becomes Ormr)

entries.title: Thorgunna
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (the head of the burnt steading is Thorgunna, replacing Hildir; she would not pay)
entries.summary: Head of the burnt steading on the starter island. She would not pay Ormr, and died at the door of her hall with her two sons.
entries.body:
Thorgunna held the steading after her husband drowned, and held it well: the bees, the sheep, the weaving, the feast at the
winter nights. When Ormr's longship came up the sound and asked for silver, she said the steading had paid the sea enough
already. She died at the door of the hall with her sons. Arnor buried her first, under the biggest stone.

FOUND: Her grave behind the hall has a stone with runes Arnor cut himself, crooked, because a smith is not a carver:
*"Arnor raised this stone for Thorgunna. She did not pay."*

entries.title: Old Aslak
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (the dead Viking in the troll's cave connects to someone met earlier: an old man in the big island's village who went there with his brother long ago and tells stories of the troll; named Aslak, his brother Hogni; his lines approved)
entries.summary: An old man in the first village of the big island, who went into the troll's hill with his brother Hogni forty winters ago and came out alone. He tells the story to anyone who will sit.
entries.tags: the troll's cave, the bronze ring, chapter 2
entries.body:
Robin's direction: the dead Viking behind the troll's lair is connected to someone the hero meets before he goes in. An old
man in the village on the big island has met the troll, and tells stories of it. He went there with his brother, long ago.

**Aslak and Hogni** (Robin named them, 2026-10-16). Forty winters ago two young brothers went into the hill to take the troll's copper. The elder,
[[person.hogni|Hogni]], wore their father's bronze ring. They struck one of the troll's young because it would not get
out of the way, and the troll came. Aslak ran. Hogni ran the other way, deeper, past the lair, and never came out. Aslak
has told it at the village fire ever since: the little ones that waddle and bonk the stone, the father who comes when they
cry, the dark past the pool. **It is the player's guidance, in an old man's voice**, and it never tells him what to do.

**When the hero comes back with the ring.** Aslak knows it at once. He does not take it. *"Keep it. He'd want it to see
daylight."* After that he has one more line, about his brother as a boy, and then he stops telling the story.

entries.title: Hogni
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (named Hogni; the story kept: he wore their father's bronze ring into the hill and never came out)
entries.summary: Aslak's elder brother, who went deeper into the troll's hill forty winters ago with their father's bronze ring, and never came out. He is the dead Viking behind the lair.
entries.tags: the troll's cave, the bronze ring
entries.body:
Bones in rotted mail, behind the troll's lair, past the ore. A bronze ring on the arm. Scratched low on the rock beside him,
as if by a man sitting down: *"Hogni. Tell Aslak to run faster."*

IN THE GAME: The dead Viking lies behind the troll's lair with the bronze ring; E takes the ring (`docs/arm-ring.md`, step 5).

entries.title: The old fisherman
entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-08 (the Game Developer's lines, ROLES.fisherman in src/village.js; Robin has not reviewed them)
entries.summary: An old man alone in a hut on a small island, who has fed himself from the sea for sixty years and teaches his fish dishes.
entries.body:
He lives alone on the smallest island with his racks and his boat, and teaches the fish dishes to anyone who sits down.

SAID: "Sit, sit. The sea has been feeding me for sixty years and it has not run dry yet." — the fisherman
SAID: "Mind the pike. Let him run when he runs, and reel when he rests, or he takes your line with him." — the fisherman

PROPOSED: He is the first person who has seen [[legend.midgardsormen|the swell]] and will say so. Once the hero has felt it
at sea, he has a new line: *"A sea going up and down with no wind on it. You felt it, then. Don't fish there."*

entries.title: The väsen
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-05 (creatures come from Norse myth and Scandinavian folklore; trolls and väsen look like the old illustrations)
entries.summary: The beings of the land, the water and the dark, as real to folk as wolves are. Never cute, never a mascot.
entries.body:
**Väsen** is the old word for the beings that share the land with people: trolls in the hills, the huldra in the forest,
Näcken in the river, the tomte in the barn, the mara at night. Folk do not think them magical. They think them *there*, the
way wolves and storms are there, and they have rules for living beside them, the way they have rules for wolves.

Robin's direction: creatures from Norse mythology and Scandinavian folklore. **Trolls and the other väsen look like the old
illustrations: hairy, heavy, long-armed, evil and careless, never goofy or smiling.** The first time a creature is slain its
card goes in the Book of Beasts, with what folk know of it.

entries.title: The mountain troll
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-05 (name, lore and mechanics in docs/beasts.md); in the game as the cave troll
entries.summary: Old as the hills and as slow to think. It hoards the mountain's ore, walks out at night, and turns to stone in daylight.
entries.game: BESTIARY troll; the troll's cave (src/cave.js); trollSeek
entries.body:
**Robin's lore:** *Trolls are old as the hills they live in and as slow to think. They hoard what the mountain holds, ore and
silver and the bones of travellers, and they cannot bear the sun: a troll caught in daylight turns to stone where it stands.
Many a strange rock on a hillside was once a troll that lingered too long.*

**What the hamlet says:** *"There is a troll in the hill cave. We leave it be and it leaves us be. Do not mine there at
night."* Folk say the ground shakes when it comes, and that fire makes it shield its eyes.

PROPOSED: The troll of the big island's cave is a father. His young are [[being.harungen|Hårungen]], and their mother is
[[being.trollmor|Trollmor]]. That is why he comes for anyone who strikes them. Behind his lair lies the dead man with the
bronze ring ([[person.hogni|Hogni]], proposed): the troll never touched the body, because trolls do not eat what has been
dead too long. Or because something about the ring kept him off. Folk disagree.

IN THE GAME: The cave troll walks out some nights, shields his eyes at a fire, turns to stone if caught provoked by
daylight, and keeps a hoard. He comes for you when his young are struck again and again, when three are killed, when he
sees you in his cave, or by a chance that grows with every ore you mine (Robin, 2026-10-16).

TRUE IN PLAY: "Do not mine there at night" is half true. He does not hear every blow of the pick. But the more ore a miner
takes, the likelier he comes, and the young who bonk at the ore are his to protect. (The Game Developer, 2026-10-16.)

entries.title: Hårungen, the troll's young
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (picked the art studio's Hårungen, the mop; the troll's young, friendly until struck; the troll senses it)
entries.summary: The cave troll's young, half the hero's height, all mop and nose. They waddle to the ore and bonk at it with their bones, and leave you be unless struck.
entries.game: UNGE, ungeAlarm (templates/game.html); the art studio's sheets troll_unge
entries.body:
Five of them live in the troll's cave. Each is born old: a scowl, warts, a crooked tooth, a mop of hair to the shoulders, a
nose past the chin, a potbelly and flat feet, a gnawed bone in the fist. They waddle to the ore rocks and the copper veins and
bonk at them with their bones, which does nothing, and they idle about, and shuffle off if you come close. Strike one, and it
turns on you, and so does every other one that saw it. Strike them often, and their father comes.

**What the hamlet says (proposed):** *"The little ones are no harm. It's their father you'll meet if you make them cry."*
And: *"Hårungen, my grandmother called them. The hairy ones."*

PROPOSED: Folk say troll young copy what they see. They bonk the ore because they have watched miners. A troll-child raised
near people can learn to be almost a person, and a person's child left in the forest can be swapped for one (the old
changeling belief). Their name, Hårungen, is the folk word for them, "the hairy ones".

entries.title: The Gape
entries.decided: in the game's Combat Arena since 2026-10-12 (the Game Developer's design and name; Robin has not reviewed it as lore)
entries.summary: A troll of the sea caves, drowned so long it is nearly all mouth. The whole top of it lifts like a lid on two rows of needle teeth.
entries.body:
From the game's `beasts.md`: a troll of the sea caves and the tide line, drowned so long that it is nearly all mouth. One
great bloodshot eye; the other socket torn and healed shut. Kelp for hair, barnacles on its back, thin arms ending in hooks,
and what is left of the last one it met still hanging between its teeth.

**What folk say (proposed):** wet drag marks up a beach and bones above the tide line. Fishermen on the western skerries say
it is what becomes of a man who drowned owing Rán gold. Approach from its blind side.

entries.title: The three-headed troll
entries.decided: in the game's Combat Arena since 2026-10-12 (the Game Developer's design and name; Robin has not reviewed it as lore)
entries.summary: The many-headed troll of the Norwegian tales: a starved giant of bone, with three heads that never look the same way.
entries.body:
The many-headed troll of the Norwegian folk tales (three heads, six, nine), drawn as if it had starved for a hundred years.
Three heads on three necks: a skull with the skin still on it; a hag on a long neck, her jaw unhinged; and a small shrivelled
one, sewn shut, that screams.

**What folk say (proposed):** in the tales each head must be cut off, and the heads quarrel. The small one gives it away by
screaming at night, so you hear it long before you see it. A troll with three heads has three times the memory, and a grudge
in each.

entries.title: The huldra
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-05 (the lore) and 2026-10-12 (the look: bright colours, a red dress, fair hair, a hollow rotten tree for a back, no tail)
entries.summary: The lady of the forest: the most beautiful woman you will ever see from the front, a hollow tree from behind. She keeps the forest's animals as a farmer keeps cattle.
entries.body:
**The lore (Robin's, from beasts.md):** *The lady of the forest. From the front she is the most beautiful woman you will see;
from behind she is a hollow tree, bark and rot. She keeps the forest's animals as a farmer keeps cattle, and a hunter who is
kind to her finds game everywhere, while one who wrongs her finds the forest turned against him. She takes husbands, and
they do not come back.*

**The look (Robin, 2026-10-12):** brighter colours, a red dress, fair hair, and the back of a hollowed rotten tree trunk.
No tail. The art studio made her a hollow oak under a floor-length dress mouldered away at the back, with moss in the hollow
and roots out of the bark.

**What folk say (proposed):** the animals go quiet and gather, then there is music, and a woman at the edge of the trees.
Be polite. Never follow her at dusk. If you see her back, say nothing about it. Charcoal burners leave her a share of their
food, and their kilns never fail.

entries.title: Näcken
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-12 (the look: river-pale, forest clothes, a lyre; he belongs in a lush forest stream, not the fells; he sits on a bank and vanishes when you come near, art studio 2026-10-14)
entries.summary: A pale man who sits by a forest stream playing a lyre so beautifully that you walk into the water to hear it closer.
entries.body:
A man pale as river stones, in forest clothes, who sits on a stream bank with a lyre. His music is the most beautiful thing
you will hear, and it draws you into the water, and the river keeps what it takes. He can take other shapes: a horse, a
floating log, a boy. Some say he taught the best players their art, for a price.

**Robin:** he belongs in a lush forest, by a stream or pool, not on the fells. He is also the way instruments come into the
game (Viking-age ones: lyre, bone flute, horn, lur).

**What folk say (proposed):** music under the sound of the water, and your feet moving on their own. Iron in the water stops
the music: throw in a knife or a nail and he sinks, ashamed. Say his name aloud and the pull breaks. He flees from church
bells. He will teach the lyre to anyone who brings him a black lamb, and plays with you until your fingers bleed.

IN THE GAME: Modelled by the art studio (on a bank with reeds, a playing loop and a vanish clip). Not in the game yet. Robin
(2026-10-14): new creatures like Näcken may show up on an island after winter.

entries.title: The draugr
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-12 (the look: the walking corpse of a Viking, a drowned one, man-sized, sword and shield; wet, with sea in him, art studio 2026-10-14)
entries.summary: The dead who would not stay dead. A drowned Viking, man-sized, wet, with his sword and his shield, who comes back for what was his.
entries.tags: väsen, the dead, mounds, the sea
entries.body:
**Robin's look:** the walking corpse of a Viking, a drowned one, man-sized, with a sword and a shield. Wet: weed on him, the
sea running off.

**The lore (from beasts.md):** a dead chieftain who would not leave his treasure. He sits in the dark of his mound on his
grave goods, swollen and black. He is as strong as ten men and smells of the sea and of rot. Grettir fought one in the saga
and barely lived, and was cursed by its eyes in the moonlight for the rest of his life.

**Two kinds of restless dead** (real belief). The *haugbúi*, the mound-dweller, stays in his mound and attacks whoever
disturbs his treasure. The *draugr*, also called the *aptrgangr*, the "after-goer", comes out and walks. The signs: a dark or
blue skin, a body that swells and grows too heavy to lift and does not rot, mist and darkness about him, a single knock at
the door, a flash of light from the eyes, and a weight on the roof at night (house-riding). In *Eyrbyggja saga* a drowned
skipper and his crew walk into the hall at Fróðá every night, dripping wet, and sit by the fire.

**What folk say (proposed):** the dead walk when they are buried wrongly, or drowned and never buried at all. Rán's drowned,
the ones she did not keep, come back up the beach on winter nights and sit by the fire in their old halls, wet. Cold iron
alone will not stop one. You wrestle him down, take his head with a sword from his own mound, burn the body to cold ashes and
throw them in the sea. A house carries the dead out through a door made for it and walled up again after, because the dead
can only come back the way they went.

IN THE GAME: Modelled (the art studio's redesign, wet). A side threat for later in the second biome (Robin, 2026-10-07).
Whether he guards a mound, a wreck, or walks out of the sea is open.

entries.title: Bysen
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-05 (makes you lose the way home) and 2026-10-12 (the look: small, tomte-like, chops slowly at trees, turns into a stump)
entries.summary: A small grey man who chops slowly at trees and turns into a stump when you come near. Who he looks at loses the way home.
entries.body:
**Robin's look:** small, tomte-like. He chops slowly at trees. Come near and he turns into a wooden stump. Axe the stump and
you get a larger amount of wood and some sort of magic piece of wood.

**The lore (from beasts.md):** the bysen was a man who moved a boundary stone, or felled a tree that was not his, and was
cursed to walk the forest forever. Now he does to others what was done to him: whoever he sets eyes on loses the way. He is not
cruel; he is lost, and lonely, and wants company.

**What folk say (proposed):** a tree stump where there was none. Turn your coat inside out and he loses sight of you. He
cannot cross running water. The wood of a bysen-stump is "lost wood": a stick of it in a boat's keel means the boat always
finds its way home. (A proposal for Robin's open "magic piece of wood".)

entries.title: The tomte
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-05 (named; lore in docs/beasts.md)
entries.summary: A small old man in a grey coat and a red cap, who has lived on the farm longer than the farmer and works at night. Never seen, only noticed.
entries.body:
**The lore (from beasts.md):** a small old man, no taller than a child, who has lived on the farm longer than the farmer. He
works at night: the animals are fed, the woodpile is stacked, the tools are sharpened. He asks only for respect, and a bowl of
porridge with butter at Yule. Forget the butter and the cow dies.

**What folk say (proposed):** small footprints in the frost by the barn; the cat watching an empty corner. He hates noise,
swearing, and iron left on his seat. A tomte comes only to a home that has been a home for a while: a roof, a hearth, a bed,
animals, and the same people sleeping there. [[person.arnor|Arnor]] says the steading had one, and that it left the night of
the fire, and that it might come back.

entries.title: The mara
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-05 (named; lore in docs/beasts.md)
entries.summary: The nightmare: a woman who rides sleepers at night, sitting on their chests until they cannot breathe. A closed house keeps her out.
entries.body:
**The lore (from beasts.md):** she comes through the keyhole as a wisp and sits on the sleeper's chest until he cannot
breathe. In the morning the horse is lathered and the sleeper tired as if he never slept. In the old tale she is a woman
cursed, and when the man plugs the keyhole she is trapped in the house with him and must take her true shape.

**What folk say (proposed):** the hearth burns blue as you lie down; the bed creaks. Steel under the pillow, a broom over the
door, or a plugged keyhole keeps her out. She rides those who sleep in the open, or in a house with a gap in its wall, or who
killed too many that day. Our word *nightmare* is her name.

entries.title: The shapeshifter
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-05 (named: a rare thing the player stumbles upon)
entries.summary: Some are born with a second skin, and some win it by a bargain. An animal that looks at your face, not your hands.
entries.body:
**The lore (from beasts.md):** some are born with a second skin, and some win it by a bargain. In the old tales a man puts on
a wolf's belt and runs the forest for nine nights, or a woman wears a swan's feathers and flies. They are not evil. They are
people, with a secret, and most of them want to be left alone.

**What folk say (proposed):** an animal with a person's eyes: it looks at your face, not your hands. Take its skin and it is
only a person. It changes back at dawn whether it wants to or not. Silver hurts it. In the sagas a man who is *hamrammr*,
"shape-strong", grows tired every evening, and his household knows not to ask where he goes.

entries.title: The valkyries
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-05 (named; lore in docs/beasts.md)
entries.summary: Odin's choosers of the slain, who ride over a battlefield deciding who dies and carrying the best to Valhalla. Never sought, never fought.
entries.body:
**The lore (from beasts.md):** Odin's maidens, armoured and mounted, who ride over the field choosing who dies and who is
carried to Valhalla to feast and fight until Ragnarök. To see one is to know a great warrior is about to die. They are not
cruel and not kind; they are the will of the gods.

**What folk say (proposed):** ravens gather, the light turns gold, a rider in the sky. Folk say a hirdman who dies well is
carried, and his fellows should be glad. A valkyrie is the one thing the gods let people see, because it is only seen by the
dying and the ones beside them, and they are not believed.

THE TENSION: Gods are never seen ([[world.faith]]). The valkyrie is the one exception folk allow, and only at a death. The
game can keep her at the edge: a rider in a sky that has just turned gold, gone by the next frame.

entries.title: The giants
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-05 (named; lore in docs/beasts.md)
entries.summary: Here before the gods: of frost, of fire and of stone, taller than a hall. Not all monsters; some are wise, and will riddle instead of fight.
entries.tags: giants, the far north, the end
entries.body:
**The lore (from beasts.md):** the giants were here before the gods, and the gods built the world from the body of one. They
are of frost, of fire and of stone, and they are the enemies of Asgard, but they are not all monsters: Mímir was wise, and
Skaði beautiful, and Þrymr only wanted a wife. All are stronger than any man, and taller than a hall.

**What folk say (proposed):** in the far north, past the Haleygs' last hall, the snow never melts and the giants live in it.
The weather is the sign: the cold deepens, the ground steams, the hills move. A wise giant beaten in a riddle gives more than
one slain. And every mountain that looks like a sleeping face is one.

entries.title: Midgardsormen, the World Serpent
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-14 (huge and mythological, appearing and moving the sea; the player meets him one day, his head rising out of the water facing the player; the jaw open and the eyes white, empty and soulless)
entries.summary: Loki's child, thrown into the sea by Odin, grown round the whole world with his tail in his mouth. When he lets go, the world ends.
entries.tags: the Serpent thread, the sea, the end, the Serpent Ring
entries.body:
**The sources.** In the Eddas he is Jörmungandr, the Midgard Serpent: the middle child of [[god.loki|Loki]] and the giantess
Angrboða, whom Odin threw into the sea round Midgard, where he grew until he lay round the whole world biting his own tail.
[[god.thor|Thor]] once had him on a hook, and the giant Hymir cut the line. At Ragnarök he lets go of his tail, the sea surges
over the land, and he and Thor kill each other. In later Norwegian belief he is the *sjøorm*, the sea serpent of Olaus Magnus
(1555): two hundred feet long, black-scaled, red-eyed, with a mane down his neck, seen only in calm, fair weather.

**Robin's decisions.** He is huge and mythological, appearing and moving the sea (2026-10-14). One day the player meets him:
his massive head comes up out of the water facing the player, the view pulled so far out the player is tiny, everything else
faded. His jaw hangs open on uneven teeth and **his eyes are white, empty and soulless** (2026-10-14, with the art studio).

**What the fishermen say.** He sleeps in the deep and turns in his sleep, and the long swell on a windless day is his
breathing. He never chases and never hunts: he is not after you, you are in his way. Never in sight of land, never in a storm,
never under a ship with the gods' luck on it (a dragon stem, an offering before sailing, a rune on the hull). The further west
you dare, the more of him you meet.

**The stages, from the game's idea bank (the Game Developer's, 2026-10-14):** 1) **the swell**, the sea moving with no wind;
2) **the coil**, a black ridge rising and sinking, longer than a longship; 3) **the head**, at dusk or in fog, the breath
hanging on the water; 4) **the wake**, one wrong wave crossing the sea, that a village on a far shore will tell of
afterwards. The book's page is the only place he is drawn whole: an old chart, the ring round a small drawn world.

**The one man he fears** (Robin, 2026-10-16). Folk say the Serpent fears and respects [[person.ormr|Ormr Midgardbane]],
and leaves him to travel the ocean without worry of storm. Some say Ormr can even call the Serpent up to rule the sea. Where
Ormr's sail is seen, the swell lies down.

PROPOSED: **Why he is restless now.** Folk link it to the empty high seat: [[person.hrolf|King Hrólf]] took the
[[thing.serpent-ring|Serpent Ring]] west to fish for him twenty winters ago, and the swell has come oftener ever since. And
why the Serpent lets [[person.ormr|Ormr]] pass, nobody knows (Robin, 2026-10-16). Every survivor he leaves tells it
differently.

entries.title: Wild boar
entries.decided: in the game's BESTIARY (Game Developer); Robin has not reviewed the text
entries.summary: Roots for acorns, keeps to the same few groves, charges hard. Freyr's beast.
entries.body:
**Folk name:** Vildsvin. **Where:** grass and oak groves, in small home ranges.

**Lore:** Boars root for acorns and keep to the same few groves. The Norse hunted them with spears and served them at the
winter feast, and the god Freyr rode a boar with golden bristles.

**The tell:** it stamps and shakes before it charges. **Drops:** boar meat; cook it at the hearth.

IN THE GAME: Strengths: charges hard and fast; its thick hide takes the first blow. Weaknesses: slow to turn; step aside as it
charges and strike its flank. The starter island's boars are young (Game Developer, 2026-10-12).

PROPOSED: One more line for the card, when the Yule boar exists: *"At Yule a boar is led into the hall and men lay their hands
on its bristles and swear what they will do in the year to come. Not all of them do it."* (Real: the *Hervarar saga*.)

entries.title: Deer
entries.decided: in the game's BESTIARY (Game Developer); Robin has not reviewed the text
entries.summary: Shy and quick, the hunter's prize. Antler for combs, hide for cloaks.
entries.body:
**Folk name:** Hjort. **Where:** open meadows and the edges of groves.

**Lore:** Shy and quick, deer are the hunter's prize. Their antlers were carved into combs and the hides made good cloaks.

**The tell:** it raises its head and freezes before it bolts. **Drops:** meat and leather.

IN THE GAME: Strengths: faster than you, and always watching. Weaknesses: timid; arrows reach it, feet do not. Herds with a
watcher; shot, it bleeds and leaves a trail.

PROPOSED: *"Four harts graze in the branches of the World Tree and gnaw at its bark. The old ones say a white one in a herd is
an omen, and nobody knows of what."*

entries.title: Wolf
entries.decided: in the game's BESTIARY (Game Developer); Robin has not reviewed the text
entries.summary: The outlaw's name. A pack comes every night; a fire keeps it off.
entries.body:
**Folk name:** Ulv. **Where:** deep forest, in packs, bolder at night.

**Lore:** The wolf was the outlaw's name and the giant wolf Fenrir will swallow the sun at the end of the world. Few beasts
were feared more.

**The tell:** it crouches low with its ears back. **Drops:** meat and a grey pelt.

IN THE GAME: A pack of three comes each night, eyes red; a fire keeps them off. Strengths: quick, relentless, never alone for
long. Weaknesses: light; a parry throws it and a shield wall stops it.

SAID: "Wolves took two sheep last moon. They come at night, from the dark wood." — a villager on the big island

entries.title: Bear
entries.decided: in the game's BESTIARY (Game Developer); Robin has not reviewed the text
entries.summary: The strongest beast of the North. Berserkers wore its skin.
entries.body:
**Folk name:** Björn. **Where:** dense forest and rocky hills.

**Lore:** The strongest beast of the North. Berserkers wore its skin and fought in its rage, and to kill one alone made a
man's name.

**The tell:** it rises on its hind legs and roars. **Drops:** meat and a bear pelt.

IN THE GAME: Strengths: enormous strength; one blow takes most of your health. Weaknesses: slow; it rears before it strikes;
fire frightens it.

PROPOSED: Folk never say the bear's real name in the forest, in case it hears. They call it *the old man*, *the honey-paw*,
*grandfather*. (Real: *björn* itself was once such a name, "the brown one", because the true name was not to be said.)

entries.title: Moose
entries.decided: in the game's BESTIARY (Game Developer); Robin has not reviewed the text
entries.summary: The king of the forest, taller than a man at the shoulder.
entries.body:
**Folk name:** Älg. **Where:** wet woods, lakesides and marsh.

**Lore:** The king of the forest. Taller than a man at the shoulder, it was hunted in deep snow when it could not run.

**The tell:** it lowers its head and paws the ground. **Drops:** a great deal of meat, and antler.

IN THE GAME: Strengths: great reach with its antlers, and it does not scare. Weaknesses: cannot turn quickly in trees; keep
a trunk between you.

entries.title: Adder
entries.decided: in the game's BESTIARY (Game Developer); Robin has not reviewed the text
entries.summary: The only venomous snake of the North. Basks on warm stones, strikes when stepped on.
entries.body:
**Folk name:** Huggorm. **Where:** sunny rocks and the edges of the beach.

**Lore:** The only venomous snake of the North. It basks on warm stones and strikes only when stepped on or cornered.

**The tell:** it coils and lifts its head. **Drops:** nothing worth keeping.

IN THE GAME: Snake blood is a cost of the claim stone. Strengths: hard to see in the grass; its bite burns. Weaknesses: short
reach and a soft body.

PROPOSED: Folk on the starter island say every adder is a tiny piece of the Serpent, and that is why its blood goes into the
claim stone's red: it binds the stone to the world's edge. Nobody can say where they heard it.

entries.title: The burnt steading
entries.decided: Robin's idea (2026-10-05): a broken village on the home island where the first friendly person is met and the first legendary Viking is heard of. Robin, 2026-10-16: the hero comes to it while the survivor, Arnor, is there scavenging and fixing what he can; he was left alive to tell the story.
entries.summary: The steading on the starter island that Ormr Midgardbane burned two winters ago. A burnt hall, a hut still whole, a plank house by the well, a palisade with gaps, and Arnor in the ruin, mending what he can.
entries.tags: chapter 1, the first home, ruins, the survivor
entries.body:
A burnt hall with its walls knocked in. A wattle hut still whole. A plank house by the well missing five walls and its roof,
which becomes the hero's first home when he mends it. A palisade with gaps. Crates to break. And [[person.arnor|Arnor]],
the smith, in the ruin when the hero comes over the rise, scavenging and fixing what he can (Robin, 2026-10-16). The dead
under the turf behind the hall.

PROPOSED: **Whose it was.** It was [[person.thorgunna|Thorgunna]]'s steading, and the folk of the big island still call it
that. Behind the hall: the graves, each with a small marker, and Thorgunna's under the biggest stone, with Arnor's crooked
runes. By the well, toppled: the steading's old claim stone (the game already has one; raising it is how the hero makes the
place his). In the smithy: Arnor's broken forge, the anvil split, which he has never mended, because he wants it seen.

PROPOSED: **Arnor's mending.** Small things show he has been at work for two winters: a door rehung on new hinges in a house
with no roof, a new bucket on the well, a shutter that closes. He fixes what he can, not what is needed.

IN THE GAME: Today the game calls it "Hildir's steading", Brokk stands by the well, and Ragnar's crew burnt it. The names
change with Robin's decision of 2026-10-16.

entries.title: The troll's cave
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-06 (copper, the troll and the cave, the arm ring from the dead Viking at the back) and 2026-10-16 (Hårungen)
entries.summary: A cave in the big island's mountain: a daylight tunnel, a pool, a chasm, copper veins, the troll's lair, and behind it, the dead Viking with the bronze ring.
entries.tags: chapter 2, the troll, copper, the arm ring
entries.game: src/cave.js; the troll's cave in templates/game.html
entries.body:
One way through from a tunnel of daylight: a hall, a hollow under a hole in the roof, a still pool, a cavern split by a chasm,
a gallery of copper veins, the [[being.bergtroll|troll]]'s lair, and behind it the dead Viking with the
[[thing.bronze-ring|bronze ring]]. [[being.harungen|Hårungen]] bonk at the ore with their bones.

The dead man is [[person.hogni|Hogni]], who went into the hill forty winters ago with his brother
[[person.aslak|Aslak]] and did not come out. Scratched low on the rock beside him, as if by a man sitting down: *"Hogni.
Tell Aslak to run faster."* Aslak tells the story of that day at the village fire on the big island, so the hero has heard
of the cave, the little ones and their father before he ever goes in (Robin's connection, 2026-10-16).

entries.title: The claim stone
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-06 (stone and berries for the red of the runes; several stones, each after the first needs a hirdman as its keeper)
entries.summary: A raised stone with your mark cut and reddened in it. It makes a place yours, and the hird gathers at it.
entries.body:
A *bautasteinn*, a raised stone, as Vikings did raise to claim and to remember. Stone, and berries for the red of the runes,
and snake blood (as built). Every stone after the first needs a hirdman to stay as its keeper.

PROPOSED: The words cut in a claim stone follow the old formula: *"[The hero's byname] raised this stone. This land is his,
and his men's."* Raising the burnt steading's own toppled stone is how the hero makes Thorgunna's land his. The berries and
the blood are for the [[being.landvaettir|land-spirits]].

entries.title: Runestones
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-06 (runestones give the odd runes; reading one is a rite)
entries.summary: Stones raised for the dead, cut with who raised them, for whom, and one deed. Some of them hold a rune that changes how a thing is done.
entries.body:
Real runestones follow one formula: *who raised the stone, for whom, and what they did*. "Tóla raised this stone for her son
Harald, Ingvar's brother. They went bravely far for gold, and in the east fed the eagle." (The Gripsholm stone.) Most are
raised by women for husbands and sons who went away and did not come back.

PROPOSED: Every runestone in the game carries one such line, generated from the names of the place and its dead, and some
carry a rune (the odd ones, Robin's). The text of a stone is the first lore a player reads, so it should be beautiful, short,
and about a person.

entries.title: Churches
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-07 (churches with friendly priests who cannot defend themselves: lucky strikes, though an army may turn up)
entries.summary: The White Christ's houses in the south: cut stone, a bell, silver on the altar, and a priest who does not fight.
entries.tags: the south, raids, the White Christ
entries.game: Village ARCH church and town; ROLES.priest
entries.body:
Cut stone, a slate roof, a bell tower at the side, silver on the altar and a priest who will not lift a hand. Robin's "lucky
strikes, though an army may turn up".

SAID: "Peace be upon this house, stranger." — a priest
SAID: "The silver on the altar is God's, not mine. He will know who took it." — a priest

PROPOSED: Folk belief says the [[being.vasen|väsen]] cannot bear church bells, so the country round a church has fewer of
them, and the folk there are less careful.

entries.title: The arm ring
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-06 (docs/arm-ring.md): runes are knowledge cut into the ring and reddened with blood; the metal is the rank (bronze, silver, twisted silver, gold, dragon)
entries.summary: Every free person wears one; the metal is the rank. Runes cut into it and reddened with the wearer's blood have power. Oaths are sworn on it.
entries.body:
Every Viking wore arm rings, jarls gave them to their men, oaths were sworn on them, and in Egil's saga runes cut and reddened
with blood had power (Robin's system, which the game never explains). **The metal is the rank: bronze, silver, twisted
silver, gold, dragon.** Every figure in the world wears its ring on the arm and is named by it in speech ("Ormr of the gold
ring").

| Ring | Coils | Where it comes from (the game) | Who wears it (the lore, proposed) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bronze | 2 | the dead Viking behind the troll's lair | free farmers, steading heads, Arnor, Aslak and Hogni's father |
| Silver | 3 | a jarl or hoard of the second biome | jarls of the new houses, captains, Önund |
| Twisted silver | 4 | later biomes | jarls of the old houses, sea-queens, the Haleygs |
| Gold | 6 | the hall in the south | sea-kings and the old royal blood: Ormr, the Skjoldings, the Scale-keepers |
| Dragon | 8 | the thing the legends are about | the king. See [[thing.serpent-ring]] |

PROPOSED: **The words of the rite.** Oaths are sworn *by Ullr's ring* (see [[god.ullr]]). When a rune is cut and reddened at the
carver's bench, the old words would be: *"I cut, I redden, I bind."* The game says none of it out loud.

entries.title: The bronze ring
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (Aslak's lines approved: the ring was the brothers' father's, worn by Hogni into the troll's hill). In the game since step 5 of docs/arm-ring.md.
entries.summary: The first ring of the game, taken from a dead man at the back of the troll's cave. Two coils, hand and foot.
entries.tags: the arm ring, the troll's cave, Aslak and Hogni
entries.body:
Two coils: the hand and the foot. The hero takes it from the dead Viking at the very back of the troll's cave, behind the
lair. The smith's taught rune comes after it.

It was [[person.hogni|Hogni]]'s, and before him his father's: a plain old bronze cuff, worn thin on the inside,
which Hogni wore into the troll's hill forty winters ago. His brother [[person.aslak|Aslak]], on the big island, knows it at
once. He will not take it back: *"Keep it. He'd want it to see daylight."* So the hero's first ring is a gift, given twice:
once by the dead, once by the living.

entries.title: Brokk, meeting him
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, rewritten 2026-10-14 after Robin's play-test)
entries.summary: Brokk's story, told once, to a stranger.
entries.speaker: person.brokk
entries.when: brokkState meet: the first time E is pressed at Brokk
lines: You live, then. Few do, from a sea like that.
Brokk. I was Hildir's smith, when there was a Hildir. Two winters back Ragnar Ironside came up the sound with a longship and left us this.
Some of ours he took for thralls. Some went with him of their own will. The rest are under the turf behind the hall.
The plank house by the well still has its bones. Put walls on it before the dark, if you mean to stay.
entries.body:
The second line is about 140 characters, a little over the limit.

ROBIN DECIDED: On 2026-10-16, Brokk is now Arnor and his story is redone; Ragnar is now Ormr Midgardbane; Hildir's name goes. These are the game's words today and stay in-game until the game takes [[line.arnor.meet]] and the others.

entries.title: Brokk, while the home lacks something
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, 2026-10-14)
entries.summary: One line for what the home still lacks: walls and roof, a hearth, a bench, something on the floor.
entries.speaker: person.brokk
entries.when: brokkState wait; the line picked by the first thing baseComfort() lacks
lines: Walls and a roof first. The nights here are not kind.
A fire in it. A roof without a fire is a cave.
A bench to work at. Hands alone make poor tools.
Something on the floor. A house is not a home until it is warm underfoot.
entries.body:
The four lines go in order of the lack: no walls, no hearth, no bench, no rug.

entries.title: Arnor, meeting him
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: Robin's start: the hero comes on Arnor in the ruin, scavenging and fixing what he can. Arnor tells it, because that is what he was left for.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState meet: the first time E is pressed at the survivor
lines: You came from the sea with less than I have. I didn't think that could be done.
Arnor. I was the smith here. Two winters back Ormr Midgardbane came up the sound and left us this.
He always leaves one. Somebody has to tell it, he said. So here I am, telling it.
The plank house by the well still has its bones. Put walls on it before the dark, if you mean to stay.
entries.body: Arnor never asks who the hero is. He has noticed there is no ring, no kin and no answer, and he lets it be.

entries.title: Arnor, the home has no walls or roof
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: The game's own line first, then two more, so it does not repeat.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState wait; baseComfort().n is 0
lines: Walls and a roof first. The nights here are not kind.
Four walls and a roof. Everything else is only weather.
I've mended three roofs here since. Nobody to sleep under them. Change that.

entries.title: Arnor, the home has no hearth
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: A smith on fire.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState wait; the home has a roof but no hearth
lines: A fire in it. A roof without a fire is a cave.
Cold iron takes no shape. Cold men neither. Give it a hearth.
He broke my forge. He didn't think to break the hearthstones. Use them.

entries.title: Arnor, the home has no bench
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: A smith on benches.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState wait; the home has a hearth but no workbench
lines: A bench to work at. Hands alone make poor tools.
At a bench I can make anything. Without one I'm a man with a hammer.
Somewhere to sit and mend things. A house where nothing is mended falls down.

entries.title: Arnor, the home has nothing on the floor
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: The last thing a home needs.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState wait; the home lacks only a rug
lines: Something on the floor. A house is not a home until it is warm underfoot.
Bare boards. Thorgunna would have laughed you out of the hall.
Put a hide down. Cold feet make a man stupid, and you've no wits to spare.

entries.title: Arnor, teaching the raft
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: The home is a home; Arnor teaches the raft and points east, after the sails.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState teach: Comfort 4 reached
lines: That is a home. Good. Sit a while. First one I've seen here in two winters.
Logs, and rope. Three logs lashed together will carry a man across the sound.
A bench on the sand, by the water. Then east, past the big island. That is where his sails went.

entries.title: Arnor, after the raft is taught
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: Said every time after, so Arnor is not a signpost.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState taught
lines: The bench on the sand. Lay the logs, and mind the sea.
Tell them on the big island you met Arnor. They'll know the rest. Everyone does.
I'll be here. Somebody has to keep the graves.

entries.title: Arnor, at the graves
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: A new situation: the hero stands among the graves behind the hall while Arnor is near. Said once.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: new: the hero stands among the graves behind the hall for a few seconds, once
lines: Thorgunna, who would not pay. Her two boys beside her. Grímhild, who kept the bees. Thorkel the boatwright.
I cut her runes myself. They're crooked. She'd have laughed at them.
You see? Somebody stands here, and I tell it. Every time. He knew I would.

entries.title: Arnor, at the shore as the hero leaves
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: A new situation from the game's start-loop.md: the survivor walks to the shore and stands there as you paddle out.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: new: the raft first launched from the starter island
lines: Go on, then. And if you hear his story told somewhere, tell them how it ends here.
East. Come back with somebody. This place could use a second voice.

entries.title: Old Aslak, at the village fire
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: Robin's connection (2026-10-16): an old man in the big island's village who went into the troll's hill with his brother long ago, and tells stories of the troll. His story is the player's guidance, in his own voice.
entries.speaker: person.aslak
entries.when: E at Old Aslak, before the ring is found; said in order over several talks
lines: My brother and I went into the troll's hill when we were young and stupid. I came out.
Little ones in there, all hair and nose. They bonk the stone with bones. Leave them be.
We didn't. One cried, and the father came. I ran for the light. Hogni ran the other way.
He had our father's ring on. It's in there still, past the big one's bed, if the troll left him an arm.

entries.title: Old Aslak, when the hero has the ring
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: A new situation: the first talk with Aslak after the bronze ring is taken from the cave.
entries.speaker: person.aslak
entries.when: new: the first talk with Aslak while the hero has the bronze ring
lines: That's his. … That's our father's ring.
Keep it. He'd want it to see daylight.
He could whistle through his fingers louder than any boy on the island. I'd forgotten that.

entries.title: The folk on Ormr and the sea
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: New pairs for villagers anywhere, carrying Robin's lore of Ormr Midgardbane: the Serpent fears him, no storm touches him, he can call the snake up.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: E at a villager at peace; one pair per villager
lines: Ormr Midgardbane. Say it quietly. They say the sea listens to him.
The storm that sank my cousin went round his ship like water round a stone.
They say the Serpent fears him. I say the Serpent has more sense than we do.
Pay him. Everybody pays him. The ones who didn't are a story now.
Every place he burns, he leaves one alive. To tell it.
So we'd know what we're paying for.

entries.title: The hamlet's folk, talking
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, FOLK_LINES, 2026-10-05 onward)
entries.summary: The nine pairs the big island's villagers say on E. Each villager has one pair.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: E at a villager of the hamlet, at peace
lines: Fair winds brought you, or foul?
The well is sweet here. Drink if you like.
Ragnar's men came by last winter. We paid them in wool and they left.
Pay, and they leave. Fight, and they burn.
My brother went east with the traders. Rivers all the way, he said.
East is trade. West is nothing but sea.
Colder north of here than you would think.
Keep a fire. Keep a roof. The rest comes.
You will find no work here, but no trouble either.
We mind our own.
The hall in the south has silver on its walls, they say. And a hundred spears round it.
Churches have less spears.
Wolves took two sheep last moon.
They come at night, from the dark wood.
You built that raft yourself? It floats, so it is a boat.
A keel next. Then you can go somewhere.
There is a troll in the hill cave. We leave it be and it leaves us be.
Do not mine there at night.
entries.body:
The game gives each villager a pair (lines 1–2, 3–4 and so on).

ROBIN DECIDED: On 2026-10-16, the raider is Ormr Midgardbane, so "Ragnar's men" becomes "Ormr's men". Nothing else changes.

entries.title: Villagers by their calling
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, ROLES in src/village.js)
entries.summary: What a villager says by their work: fisherman, priest, guard, merchant, farmer, fisher, smith, weaver, elder, child, thrall.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: E at a villager of a generated village, by their calling
lines: (fisherman) Sit, sit. The sea has been feeding me for sixty years and it has not run dry yet.
(priest) Peace be upon this house, stranger.
(priest) The silver on the altar is God's, not mine. He will know who took it.
(guard) Keep your blade sheathed inside the walls.
(guard) The jarl sees everything from his hall.
(merchant) Wool, salt, iron. What have you got?
(merchant) Silver by weight, friend. We take no promises.
(farmer) The barley came in well this year.
(farmer) Mind the goat: she butts.
(fisher) The herring run at dawn, out past the skerry.
(fisher) That boat has crossed worse water than this.
(smith) Copper is soft. Bring me bog iron and I will show you steel.
(smith) My bench is yours if you leave it as you found it.
(weaver) Wool from our own sheep. Feel it.
(weaver) The loom took a winter to build.
(elder) Ragnar's men came once. They will come again.
(elder) My father raised the stone by the gate.
(child) Are you a Viking?
(child) I found a bird's nest with four eggs!
(thrall) ...
(thrall) I was taken from the south. This is home now.
entries.body:
The fisherman's other three lines teach his dishes and are recorded in [[person.fisherman]]. The calling in brackets is the
key; the game has them as lists by calling.

ROBIN DECIDED: On 2026-10-16, the elder's "Ragnar's men came once" becomes "Ormr's men came once".

entries.title: The folk, after a blade is drawn
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, WARY_LINES)
entries.summary: A place made uneasy by a drawn blade.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: the place's unease level is low (a blade drawn, nothing taken)
lines: Keep that blade where it is.
You frightened the children.
We want no trouble here.

entries.title: The folk, after a raid
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, RAIDED_LINES)
entries.summary: A place the hero has raided.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: the place has been raided by the hero
lines: You again. Take what you want and go.
We have nothing left. You saw to that.
The jarl will hear of this. Everyone will.

entries.title: The folk, cowering during a raid
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, COWER_LINES)
entries.summary: Said by a villager hiding while the raid goes on.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: a raid is on and the villager is hiding
lines: Take it. Take all of it.
Not the children.
We have nothing. Nothing.
Gods, not us.
Leave us be.

entries.title: The folk, burnt out
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, HOMELESS_LINES)
entries.summary: A villager whose house has burned.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: the villager's house is burnt
lines: It is gone. All of it.
Where are we to sleep now?
My father built that house.

entries.title: The folk, mourning someone the hero killed
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, mournLines)
entries.summary: Names the last person the hero killed in this place. {dead} is that name; {count} is how many.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: someone in this place has been killed by the hero
lines: You killed {dead}.
{dead} never lifted a hand to you.
{count} of us. {count}.
There is blood on you. Go.
entries.body: The game says the second line when one is dead and the third when more are.
